chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqa (RA) said: Muhammad ibn Harun al-Sufi said: 'Ubays Allah ibn Musa Abu Trab al-Royani said, on the authority of Abd al-'Azim ibn Abd Allah al-Hasani, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abu Mahmud, who said: I asked al-Rida (AS): 'O son of the Messenger of Allah, what do you say about the tradition that people narrate from the Messenger of Allah (SAW) that he said: 'Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, descends every night to the lowest heaven?'

He (AS) replied: 'May Allah curse those who alter words from their places! By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (SAW) did not say it that way. Rather, he (SAW) said: Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, sends down an angel to the lowest heaven every night during the last third, and on Friday night at the beginning of the night. He commands him, so he calls out: Is there any supplicant so I may grant his wish? Is there any repentant so I may forgive him? Is there any seeker of forgiveness so I may forgive him? O seeker of good, come forward! O seeker of evil, hold back! He continues calling with this until dawn breaks. When dawn breaks, he returns to his place in the realm of heaven.' My father related this to me from my grandfather, from the Messenger of Allah (SAW).
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Allah's descent and the angel's descent according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) refutes the anthropomorphic view of Allah descending by clarifying that it is an angel who descends to the lowest heaven during the last third of the night to announce forgiveness, rather than the Divine Essence itself. This distinction is central to the Shia theological principle of *tanzih* (divine transcendence), preserving Allah's immateriality against those who 'alter the words from their proper places' (*al-muharrifun*). The narration emphasizes that this nightly call for repentance ceases at dawn, highlighting the specific temporal window for divine mercy without implying physical movement of God.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 7. `Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Imran al-Daqqa (RA) said: Muhhamd ibn Huran al-Suri said: `Ubays Allah ibn Musa Abu Talib al-Rawyani said, on the authority of `Abd al-`Azim ibn `Abd Allah al-Hasani, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Abu Mahmud that I asked al-Rida (AS): “O son of the Messenger of Allah! What do you say about the tradition which people narrate from the Messenger of Allah (SA) that he said: `Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, comes down from the heaven of this world every night?’”

Thus, he (AS) replied, May the curse of Allah be upon those who alter words from their place! By Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, sends down an angel from heaven to this world during the third part of every night, and the first part of Friday night. Hence, He commands him, so he calls, “Is there any supplicant on whom I can bestow his wish? Is there anyone who is repenting so that I can forgive him? Is there anyone seeking forgiveness so that I may forgive him? O seekers of goodness, come! O seekers of evil, abstain!” He constantly proclaims this till dawn breaks. When dawn breaks, he return to his place in the realm of heaven. My father related to me this on the authority of my grandfather from the Messenger of Allah (SA).
